cause_quote: #104567's final revision added `// Google requires enum entries as strings even when the declared schema type is numeric or boolean. Keep the type intact...` and mapped `const` to `cleaned.enum = cleanGeminiEnumValues([value])` without retyping, so a boolean literal became `{"type":"boolean","enum":["true"]}`.
user_saw: Every Gemini or Vertex turn that exposed the built-in read tool failed with HTTP 400 "enum: only allowed for STRING type".
summary: The Gemini schema cleaner now keeps stringified const/enum values only on string or untyped schemas and drops the enum (keeping the type) for boolean/numeric schemas.
reasoning: The enum/const handling that emits string enums on non-string types was written by #104567 (its first commit message even notes Gemini only accepts enum on string-typed schemas, but the final revision kept the declared type); later commits (f16e8bc refactor, 5eab3f5 scalar types) only moved or left it unchanged. The read tool's `optional: Type.Literal(true)` parameter (from #126262, 2026-08-20) is the caller that hit it. Medium confidence because #185581 (2026-11-02) suggests Gemini-path requests with this shape were being sent without a reported 400 until 2026-11-10, so a provider-side enforcement change (latent) cannot be ruled out, and the fix was verified only against a stand-in.
